title: How can two copies of a trapezium give its area?
description: Two copies of a trapezium are joined along a slanting side, and they fit into one parallelogram. Its base is the two parallel sides side by side, so its area is that base times the height, and the trapezium is half of it. Keeko doubts that the joined copies make a parallelogram and wonders if they make a six sided figure.
teaching_notes: One idea: two copies of a trapezium make a parallelogram whose base is the sum of the parallel sides, so the trapezium is half of it. Watch for students who give the area of the parallelogram as the area of the trapezium.

source: Finding the area of a trapezium using two copies of the trapezium joined along a slanting side
video_script.why: The child knows the area of a parallelogram and here sees why the trapezium is half of the two parallel sides added, times the height.
video_script.substitution: Numbers for the book's trapezium: parallel sides 7 cm and 11 cm and height 6 cm.
video_script.anchor: two copies of the trapezium, one turned half way round and joined to the other along a slanting side
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the two joined copies make a six sided figure, because each copy has a slanting side that could bend at the join. The two angles along the joined side add up to a straight angle, so the edges run straight and the shape has four sides.
video_script.payoff_line: The trapezium covers fifty four square centimetres.
maths_rules: trapezium: parallel sides 7 cm and 11 cm, height 6 cm
two copies joined along a slanting side make a parallelogram with base 7 + 11 = 18 cm and height 6 cm
trapezium = half of the parallelogram: 108 / 2 = 54 cm2
the two angles along the joined side add up to 180, so the joined edges are straight and the shape has four sides
video_script.design: One trapezium and its turned copy stay all video. The copy turns half way round and joins the first along a slanting side into a parallelogram, with the 7 and the 11 along its base. Keeko's six sided picture is drawn beside it.

narration: <bookmark mark='para'/>Step one, the joined shape is a parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='base'/>Its base holds the seven of one copy and the eleven of the other. The base is seven plus eleven, eighteen centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: area of parallelogram = base × height = 18 × 6 = 108 cm²

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, find the area of the parallelogram. Area is base times height, eighteen times six.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That gives one hundred eight square centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step three, take half, because the parallelogram is made of two equal trapeziums.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>One hundred eight divided by two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: area of the trapezium = 54 cm²
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The trapezium covers fifty four square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='one'/>That is the area of one copy, half of the joined shape.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the joined copies make a six sided figure, with a bend at the join.
<bookmark mark='angles'/>But the two angles meeting along the joined side add up to a straight angle. This is because the top and bottom are parallel.
<bookmark mark='straight'/>Each long edge runs straight, with no bend. The shape has four sides and it is a parallelogram.
